reference_consistency_warnings.detail: C.11 says name=value generic arguments are admitted, but its normative return-item production has no equals binder and the preceding disambiguation sentence classifies an attribute= opener as a derivation. The grammar preserves the existing base-sensitive overlap via derivation-attribute-list rather than inventing a new canonical spelling.

The forall section says the contextual form is type-level only, while a Rank-2 example returns a forall-prefixed anonymous function literal. The grammar retains the pre-existing anonymous-function forall form and treats forall as contextual rather than hard-reserved.

implementation_checks_not_revalidated: alpha parser implementation trace for typed-collection-literal / typed-collection-literal-guard
runtime/parser rejection behavior for reserved future spellings
actual parser support for the new export/refinement/associated-type productions
notes: The language reference is authoritative. Grammar support is driven by active normative grammar and explicit reserved-future declarations; examples do not enable or disable productions.

forall was removed from hard-reserved-word and added to the contextual-keyword registry; contextual spellings remain lexically available as identifiers and are parser-reclassified only in their defined contexts.
self now has an explicit class-method contextual guard, and refinement candidate _ has an explicit refinement-predicate contextual guard.
src/export.fol and srclib/exports/export.fol now share export-surface-file syntax. Their filesystem location determines standalone versus project-local export semantics.
annotation map keys now admit qualified-name so @co.dap.export packages={hr.employee:{recurse=true}} can be collected by the generic metadata grammar.
co.lang.refinementType declarations and co.lang.associatedType signature requirements/module bindings are now represented explicitly.
The pre-declared glyph registry is now exactly ∪ and ∩, and both are active left-associative precedence-500 infix operators between multiplicative and additive precedence levels.
Appendix C EBNF blocks remain textually identical to their corresponding productions in the consolidated grammar.
The old Disclaimer/example-gating policy has been removed from the grammar commentary; explicit specification status now determines reserved-future handling.
The prior validation JSON did not describe the uploaded folang(10).ebnf exactly (its stored grammar SHA/count were stale); this file was regenerated from the aligned grammar and current reference.
